properties.name: A durable design knows its own name, and remembers it across opens
properties.statement: A design that composes with others must have a stable identity of its own, remembered beside the store rather than supplied on each open. Found while building cap:mirror-surface on 2026-07-25: every reflow2 graph carried the same hardcoded graph_id, so no design could tell another design from itself — mirroring had to refuse a surface whose source id equalled its own, and with one constant that check could never pass. `open_in_memory_as` fixed it for library and test use; the durable case is unsolved and is deliberately not half-built, because the id namespaces every stored key: an on-disk graph reopened under a different name would find nothing, and one reopened under the DEFAULT name after being created with another would silently present an empty design. So identity has to live where the provenance stamp already lives (the sidecar beside the store), be written once at creation, and be REFUSED rather than defaulted when a later open disagrees with it — the same shape as the schema stamp refusing a graph a binary cannot read in full. Two consequences follow. Identity must be stable across machines, or the same design mirrored from two places reads as two designs; and it must be distinct by default, since two projects both called the design's default name would mirror into each other and the collision guard would report every node as a clash. This is rule:no-foreclosure item 5 arriving as real work rather than as a hypothetical.
